issues.title: fix(aqwa-backend): align CRLF/LF line endings between generate_single and generate_modular
issues.body:
## Context

Surfaced during workspace-hub [#2614](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/workspace-hub/issues/2614) Cat C fix ([digitalmodel#551](https://github.com/vamseeachanta/digitalmodel/pull/551), merged \`d6a42770\`).

## Defect

\`AQWABackend.generate_single()\` writes CRLF line endings via \`newline=''\` semantics; \`AQWABackend.generate_modular()\` uses \`Path.write_text(...)\` which normalizes to LF. The two paths produce byte-different output.

## Why this is latent (not currently breaking)

The current test \`test_modular_concatenation_matches_single\` strips empty lines and compares stripped text, so the line-ending difference doesn't break the assertion. But any future byte-equality assertion (or downstream tooling that's CRLF-sensitive) will trip on it.

## Proposed fix

Pick one and align both paths:
- (a) Both write CRLF (matches \`generate_single\` current behavior — likely matches AQWA Workbench export convention)
- (b) Both write LF (matches \`generate_modular\` current behavior — POSIX-friendly)

Confirm canonical choice by checking what AQWA itself emits as native output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both \`generate_single\` and \`generate_modular\` produce byte-identical output for the same inputs (excluding any explicit per-deck filename/header differences)
- [ ] A new test asserts byte-equality (not just stripped-text equality)
- [ ] Existing \`test_modular_concatenation_matches_single\` continues to pass

## Files likely affected
- \`src/digitalmodel/hydrodynamics/diffraction/aqwa_backend.py\`
- \`tests/hydrodynamics/diffraction/test_aqwa_backend.py\`
issues.display_title: fix(aqwa-backend): align CRLF/LF line endings between generate_single and generate_modular

issues.body:
## WRK-131: Passing ship analysis for moored vessels — AQWA-based force calculation and mooring response

**Status:** blocked | **Priority:** high | **Category:** engineering/marine
**Complexity:** complex | **Machine:** orcaflex-license-machine

---

<details><summary>🔨 Implementation Summary</summary>

Not yet available

</details>

<details><summary>📋 Plan</summary>

# Passing Ship Analysis for Moored Vessels

## What
Build a passing ship analysis capability for moored vessels. Calculate hydrodynamic forces on a moored vessel due to a passing ship (surge, sway, yaw), evaluate mooring line tensions under passing ship events, and generate standardized reports. Covers perpendicular and parallel passing cases, with/without wind, at varying speeds and distances.

## Why
- Passing ship effects are a critical design case for port/terminal mooring systems
- ~15+ historical projects demonstrate recurring demand for this analysis type
- Currently relies on standalone Excel tool (`PassingShipForceCalculator.xlsm`) and manual AQWA runs
- Standardizing into the digitalmodel framework enables parametric studies, consistent reporting, and reuse

## Resources (local, not in repo)
- **Tool**: `G:\ACMA Tool\Passing Ships\` — existing passing ship force calculator (Excel-based)
- **Archive**: `R:\Archive - Drive J\` — ~15+ past project folders with AQWA models, reports, and results
- **Key tool files**: `PassingShipForceCalculator.xlsm` (force calculation), `PassingShipForceCalculator 3.7 knot.xlsm` (speed variant)
- **Output examples**: Line tension plots at various passing speeds (3.0 knot, 3.7 knot), mooring line groups (1-6, 7-12)

## Technical Scope
1. **Passing ship force model** — hydrodynamic interaction forces (surge, sway, yaw) as function of:
   - Passing ship speed, size (displacement, length, beam, draft)
   - Moored vessel dimensions
   - Separation distance (lateral)
   - Water depth / depth-to-draft ratio
   - Passing angle (parallel, perpendicular, oblique)
2. **Mooring response** — time-domain mooring analysis with passing ship force time history:
   - Line tensions per mooring line
   - Vessel motions (surge, sway, yaw excursions)
   - Fender loads
   - Combined with wind, current, wave (with/without passing vessel scenarios)
3. **Analysis cases** — parametric matrix:
   - Wind with passing vessel / wind without passing vessel
   - Perpendicular passing / parallel passing
   - Multiple passing speeds
   - Short ship / long ship variants
4. **PassingShipForceCalculator extraction** — reverse-engineer the Excel tool logic into Python
5. **AQWA integration** — passing ship force application in AQWA mooring analysis (or OrcaFlex equivalent)
6. **Reporting** — standardized HTML report per WRK-129 convention

## PassingShipSpec — Analysis Specification
Create a `PassingShipSpec` (similar to `DiffractionSpec` pattern) that fully defines a passing ship analysis:
- **Moored vessel**: hull geometry, mooring arrangement, loading condition, RAOs
- **Passing ship**: type, displacement, LOA, beam, draft, speed, track (distance, angle)
- **Environment**: water depth, wind speed/direction, current, wave conditions
- **Analysis matrix**: cases (with/without wind, with/without passing, speeds, angles)
- **Output requests**: line tensions, vessel motions, fender loads, force time histories
- Spec format: YAML (`spec.yml`), validated by Pydantic schema, drives automated analysis pipeline

## Benchmarking — 5-7 Historical Projects
Reproduce 5-7 past passing ship projects from `R:\Archive - Drive J\` to validate the new implementation:
1. Extract original analysis inputs (vessel data, mooring layout, passing ship parameters, environmental conditions)

</details>

<details><summary>✅ Acceptance Criteria</summary>

- [x] `PassingShipSpec` Pydantic schema defined and validated
- [x] Passing ship force calculation implemented in Python (from Excel tool extraction)
- [x] Force time history generation for given passing scenario (speed, distance, ship size)
- [ ] Mooring response analysis with passing ship forces (line tensions, motions)
- [ ] Parametric study capability (speed × distance × wind × passing angle matrix)
- [ ] 5-7 benchmark cases reproduced from historical projects, results within tolerance
- [ ] Each benchmark has sanitized `spec.yml` in `docs/domains/orcaflex/passing_ship/`
- [ ] Standardized HTML report with force plots, tension envelopes, motion time histories
- [x] Integration with existing hydrodynamics module

issues.body:
## Summary
Standardize the canonical OpenFOAM baseline for portable engineering work, using repo-tracked docs, scripts, example cases, and validation.

Part of #1782.
Primary reference: #25.
Supports downstream work such as #1268.

## Motivation
OpenFOAM is already CLI-native, but the baseline workflow is not yet fully encoded as a portable artifact bundle. We need a declared version target, canonical entrypoints, and a smoke validation path.

## Scope
Create the baseline OpenFOAM portability package in workspace-hub.

Expected deliverables:
- baseline docs
- run/validation entrypoints
- minimal smoke example
- troubleshooting guidance
- shared skill update if reusable guidance is improved

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] baseline doc declares the target fork/version explicitly (default: ESI/OpenFOAM.com v2312 unless changed by decision)
- [ ] canonical runner command(s) are documented
- [ ] minimal smoke case exists under a reproducible repo-tracked path
- [ ] validator produces pass/fail output with explicit checks
- [ ] common failure modes and version/fork mismatches are documented
- [ ] workflow can be executed on the canonical engineering host with documented prerequisites

## Notes
Implementation should prefer:
- explicit version detection and fail-fast behavior
- repo-tracked wrappers over tribal command memory
- logs/results/validation outputs in predictable locations

issues.body:
## Context

Split from vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2393 (v1 closed after MAJOR×2 cross-provider review flagged scope creep + storage-authority ambiguity + AC-vs-test gaps).

## Problem

Build the actual embeddings index using the model chosen in vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2403. This issue focuses on build + query, with a resolved single-authority storage tier.

## Deliverable

- Build script: `scripts/knowledge/build_embeddings_index.py` (incremental, idempotent).
- Query CLI: `scripts/knowledge/query_embeddings.py`.
- Storage: single authoritative tier per operating-model §7 — **decided in plan**, not left ambiguous.
- Manifest (git-tracked): `data/document-index/embeddings-manifest.yaml`.
- `sha256:`-only `doc_key` enforcement at build and query time (per operating-model §3).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All doc_keys in the index validated as `sha256:<hex>` per §3 — enforced and tested
- [ ] Single authoritative storage tier declared in plan (repo-local OR shared-mount, not both)
- [ ] p95 query latency < 2s — measured via `tests/knowledge/test_query_latency.py` (not manual)
- [ ] Row-count + model-pin + refresh-timestamp in `embeddings-manifest.yaml`
- [ ] Cost-cap guardrail has a concrete implementing file + test
- [ ] Nightly cron wired in `config/scheduled-tasks/schedule-tasks.yaml`
- [ ] Threat model section: cloud-API secret sourcing, mount-path validation, cache-poisoning protection

## Dependencies

- **Hard depends on: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2403** (model choice must be made first)
- Depends on: vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#23 (`doc_key` in wiki frontmatter), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2361, vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2362
- Blocks: vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2394 (retrieval-augmented planner), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2400 (MCP wiki_search tool)

## Scope boundaries

- **In scope:** build, query, manifest, cost-cap, cron, secrets, threat model.
- **Out of scope:** downstream consumers (planner, MCP server) — live in their own issues.

## Context
Metadata-only discovery of `/mnt/ace-data` raw-like stores identified several high-value offshore/energy source families that are not directly covered by existing llm-wiki completion plans:

- `/mnt/ace-data/client_projects/energy_bsee/raw_data` — 10 files (PDF/XLSX/DOCX/ZIP), BSEE/offshore well data descriptions and sample permit/activity material.
- `/mnt/ace-data/worldenergydata/data/modules/hse/raw` — 97 files / 7 dirs, OSHA/HSE CSV/TXT/ZIP datasets and metadata.
- `/mnt/ace-data/frontierdeepwater/data/raw` — 4 files / 1 dir, offshore magazine/heavy-lift/pipelay source material.

Focused duplicate searches found no direct open issue for `energy_bsee raw_data`, `worldenergydata hse llm-wiki`, or `frontierdeepwater llm-wiki`. Existing adjacent anchors remain vamseeachanta/llm-wiki#13 (roadmap), vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2392 (coverage-gap detector), and vamseeachanta/workspace-hub#2487 (raw-data-to-readiness spine).

## v2 adversarial review — DOUBLE MAJOR

v2 pushed at `5db2c0cbf` on branch `plan/issue-2364-batch-pack-1`. Fresh cross-review against fixed infra.

### Verdicts
| Provider | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Claude | **MAJOR** (2 P2s + 7 P3s) |
| Gemini | **MAJOR** (1 P1) |
| Codex | UNAVAILABLE (#2479) |

### v2 resolved r1 P1s + most P2s
- **Forbidden-path**: clause quoted verbatim (`config/**`, `.claude/**`, `tests/**`, `scripts/**`). Runner relocated to `docs/reports/batch-pack-1-runner.py`; tests to `docs/reports/batch-pack-1-runner-tests.py`.
- **Planner rationalization deleted.**
- **Domain classifier**: all 40 entries have `tags: None` — tag-based rules dead; v2 uses host-regex + notes-keywords only (enumerated).
- **120-char dry-run**: 25/40 pass, 15/40 insufficient — split reasonable.
- **`noaa-ndbc` → `noaa_ndbc`**: fixture id corrected (hyphen → underscore, matching registry).
- **Maritime-law**: added as 4th allowed `target_wiki_domain` with `out-of-scope-for-promotion: true`.

### Gemini's v2 finding (NEW P1)

**Regex-based YAML patching is fragile (data-corruption risk).** v2 dropped `ruamel.yaml` (not in `pyproject.toml`) and substituted 'scoped two-key text-patch with structural-diff verification'. Gemini flags: anchored regex on YAML will corrupt the file if there are commented lines, multi-line strings, or unexpected whitespace. **Surgical fix:** two options — (a) ADD `ruamel.yaml` as a new dep (small, standard lib for round-trip YAML), OR (b) write a companion `online-resource-registry.processed.yaml` overlay file that doesn't require in-place patching of the canonical registry.

### Claude's v2 findings

1. **[P2] Registry write-back idempotency tested only at report layer.** Anchored regex appends a second `processed: true` on re-run unless runner pre-checks. **Fix:** pre-write guard + byte-diff AC test.
2. **[P2] Wall-clock test flakes on CI.** `test_duplicate_check_wall_clock_under_budget` asserts <30s over 19,191 pages — slow runners will flake. **Fix:** gate behind `@pytest.mark.perf` or env var.
3. **[P2] Test sys.path for hyphenated runner.** Tests at `docs/reports/batch-pack-1-runner-tests.py` must import runner at hyphenated `batch-pack-1-runner.py`. Hyphen-path pattern AGAIN — see `feedback_llm_wiki_hyphen_module_path_pattern`. **Fix:** rename to underscore OR specify `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` mechanism.

### Claude P3s
- Registry patch atomicity (temp+rename)
- `processed_date` timezone unspecified (UTC+iso format needed)
- Classifier-precedence tests incomplete
- Stub frontmatter schema not enumerated
- Deliverable vs AC disagree on maritime-law counting
- Forbidden-path guard regex could be tightened

### Next action
**v3 needed** — Gemini's P1 (regex YAML) is the blocker; Claude's P2s are surgical. Recommend adding `ruamel.yaml` as a dep + keeping the structural verification approach.

v2 pushed at 5db2c0cbf on branch plan/issue-2364-batch-pack-1. Fresh cross-review against fixed infra.

Verdicts

Provider Verdict
Claude MAJOR (2 P2s + 7 P3s)
Gemini MAJOR (1 P1)
Codex UNAVAILABLE (#2479)

v2 resolved r1 P1s + most P2s

  • Forbidden-path: clause quoted verbatim (config/**, .claude/**, tests/**, scripts/**). Runner relocated to docs/reports/batch-pack-1-runner.py; tests to docs/reports/batch-pack-1-runner-tests.py.
  • Planner rationalization deleted.
  • Domain classifier: all 40 entries have tags: None — tag-based rules dead; v2 uses host-regex + notes-keywords only (enumerated).
  • 120-char dry-run: 25/40 pass, 15/40 insufficient — split reasonable.
  • noaa-ndbc → noaa_ndbc: fixture id corrected (hyphen → underscore, matching registry).
  • Maritime-law: added as 4th allowed target_wiki_domain with out-of-scope-for-promotion: true.

Gemini's v2 finding (NEW P1)

Regex-based YAML patching is fragile (data-corruption risk). v2 dropped ruamel.yaml (not in pyproject.toml) and substituted 'scoped two-key text-patch with structural-diff verification'. Gemini flags: anchored regex on YAML will corrupt the file if there are commented lines, multi-line strings, or unexpected whitespace. Surgical fix: two options — (a) ADD ruamel.yaml as a new dep (small, standard lib for round-trip YAML), OR (b) write a companion online-resource-registry.processed.yaml overlay file that doesn't require in-place patching of the canonical registry.

Claude's v2 findings

  1. [P2] Registry write-back idempotency tested only at report layer. Anchored regex appends a second processed: true on re-run unless runner pre-checks. Fix: pre-write guard + byte-diff AC test.
  2. [P2] Wall-clock test flakes on CI. test_duplicate_check_wall_clock_under_budget asserts <30s over 19,191 pages — slow runners will flake. Fix: gate behind @pytest.mark.perf or env var.
  3. [P2] Test sys.path for hyphenated runner. Tests at docs/reports/batch-pack-1-runner-tests.py must import runner at hyphenated batch-pack-1-runner.py. Hyphen-path pattern AGAIN — see feedback_llm_wiki_hyphen_module_path_pattern. Fix: rename to underscore OR specify importlib.util.spec_from_file_location mechanism.

Claude P3s

  • Registry patch atomicity (temp+rename)
  • processed_date timezone unspecified (UTC+iso format needed)
  • Classifier-precedence tests incomplete
  • Stub frontmatter schema not enumerated
  • Deliverable vs AC disagree on maritime-law counting
  • Forbidden-path guard regex could be tightened

Next action

v3 needed — Gemini's P1 (regex YAML) is the blocker; Claude's P2s are surgical. Recommend adding ruamel.yaml as a dep + keeping the structural verification approach.

Branch: `plan/issue-2364-batch-pack-1` @ `de71883f0`
Plan path: `docs/plans/2026-04-23-issue-2364-batch-pack-1-api-standards-portal-promotion.md`

- Source `data/document-index/online-resource-registry.yaml` stays read-only

- Determinism: `processed[]` sorted by `id`; `processed_date` carried forward so reruns are byte-identical (after stripping top-level `generated_at`)

- **Eliminates Gemini r2 P1 entirely** (no regex on YAML, no in-place mutation, no new dep)
